title: note: MCP 2026-07-28 verified spec facts for aaif-51g — statelessness's operational tail
description:
Verified live against the final spec on 2026-07-31 (spec postdates model
training data — every claim below was fetched, not recalled). Sources:
/specification/2026-07-28/{changelog,basic/index,basic/transports/streamable-http,
server/tools,basic/authorization} + schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts.

All PUBLIC spec facts. Relevant to aaif-51g ('Earned Autonomy') because they are
the operational tail of the same statelessness turn the whitepaper is built on.

## The strongest one: statelessness made retries non-idempotent

- SSE stream resumability is REMOVED. Transport spec: "Resumable SSE streams via
  Last-Event-ID are not supported."
- Changelog major 9: a broken response stream loses the in-flight request, and
  clients MUST re-issue it as a NEW request with a NEW request id.
- Consequence: a dropped connection mid-tools/call is now a RE-EXECUTION. A
  non-idempotent tool (charge/checkout/send) can double-fire on an ordinary
  network blip — and with sessions and SSE event ids both gone, the server has
  no protocol-level handle left to dedupe on. Idempotency moves to the
  application, uninstrumented, by default.
- Governance angle: the spec removed the mechanism that used to make this safe
  without adding a required replacement. That is a measurable autonomy/
  accountability gap, not just a migration chore.

## Deprecation and removal happened side by side (easy to misread)

Roots, Sampling, Logging are DEPRECATED with a >=12-month window, but three
things were REMOVED outright in the same release (changelog major 5):
- `logging/setLevel`
- `notifications/roots/list_changed`
- `ping`
Log level now travels per-request as io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel in _meta,
and "servers MUST NOT emit notifications/message for requests that did not
include this field" — so an upgrade without that field goes SILENTLY dark on
logs. Reading "deprecated, still works" as "nothing broke" is the trap.

## Other confirmed specifics

- Closing the SSE response stream MUST be treated as cancellation of that request.
- MCP-Protocol-Version header REQUIRED on every POST and MUST match the _meta
  value; mismatch => HeaderMismatch -32020 (renumbered from -32001).
- Mcp-Method required on all requests; Mcp-Name on tools/call, resources/read,
  prompts/get.
- _meta required fields: protocolVersion YES, clientCapabilities YES,
  clientInfo NO (but clients SHOULD send it). Servers SHOULD send serverInfo in
  every result's _meta. Missing required capability => -32021.
- Tool list MUST NOT vary per-connection, but MAY vary by the authorization
  presented on the request — the rule that keeps per-user tool filtering legal
  after sessions died. Pairs with cacheScope: private.
- ttlMs + cacheScope are REQUIRED (CacheableResult), not optional.
- x-mcp-header: new; mirrors tool params into Mcp-Param-{Name} HTTP headers for
  gateway routing. Spec WARNING: do not mark secrets/PII, header values are
  visible to intermediaries.
- $ref: implementations MUST NOT auto-dereference network URIs; SHOULD bound
  depth / subschema count / validation time.
- inputSchema is still pinned to type:"object" at the root (schema.ts:1997);
  outputSchema is unconstrained (schema.ts:2005).
- Resource-not-found -32002 -> -32602; clients SHOULD still accept -32002 from
  older servers.
- Authorization: AS SHOULD include iss, client MUST validate; if the AS
  advertises authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported=true and iss is
  ABSENT, the client MUST reject. Spec states a future revision is expected to
  upgrade AS inclusion from SHOULD to MUST. DCR deprecated in favor of CIMD.
- server/tools now carries a non-normative "Stateful Tools" section documenting
  the explicit-handle pattern (authorization / opacity / lifetime / expiry) —
  citable primary source for the handle-lifecycle argument.
- Four Tier 1 SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Go, C#) shipped 2026-07-28 support;
  Rust is beta.

title: PRIVACY: tailnet IP + named private host in TRACKED files of this PUBLIC repo (since 2026-07-01)
description:
## Context

Found during the 2026-08-01 tutorial-readiness review. `submissions/2026-mcp-governance-whitepaper/experiment/harness/` is **tracked** (87 files tracked in that folder, NOT gitignored) in this **public** repo and contains named private infrastructure.

This violates CLAUDE.md's explicit rule: *"Named infra + genuine secrets (keys, tailnet IPs, Asana IDs) live only in `.local/`"* and *"Generalize Zig's private infra out of public refs — refer to a self-hosted gateway / a local-model box / a private mesh in generic terms rather than by their private machine names."*

## Steps to Reproduce

```
cd ~/aaif
git grep -nE '100\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[0-1][0-9]|12[0-7])\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+|ssh pico|exp-keys'
```

Returns ~10 hits across `experiment/harness/run_ablation.sh` and `run_ablation_matrix.sh`:
- `http://100.72.47.4:25001/mcp` and `:25003` — a **tailnet IP** (100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT)
- `ssh pico` — the private gateway host **by name**, ~6 occurrences
- `/tmp/exp-keys.json` — names the key-material path (the file itself is NOT committed)

First commit carrying the IP: `73ff61c`, **2026-07-01** — public for roughly a month.

## Severity — real but bounded

- ✅ **No literal secrets are committed.** Keys are read at runtime from pico; scanned clean for `sk-*` and inline api-key assignments.
- ⚠️ A tailnet IP is not internet-routable, so practical exploitability is low. The problem is disclosure of named infra and topology against a stated rule, not an open door.

## Decision needed from Zig — NOT taken unilaterally

Scrubbing the working tree is easy. **History is the question**, and rewriting pushed history on a public repo with a second writer is exactly what the shared-tree rule warns about. Options:

1. **Scrub forward only** — parameterize the harness now (`$GATEWAY_HOST`, `$MCP_URI` from env), leave history. Lowest risk; the IP stays in old commits.
2. **Scrub + rewrite history** (filter-repo). Removes it properly; requires a force-push to a public repo and coordination with any other clone.
3. **Untrack the experiment folder** (gitignore it, per the submissions-stay-local policy aaif-983 cites) and keep it local only.

Option 3 may be cleanest since the folder is a build workspace rather than a deliverable — but it interacts with aaif-51g, which needs a PUBLISHABLE reproducible harness regardless (see that bead's reproducibility gap).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Zig picks the history disposition (forward-scrub / rewrite / untrack).
- [ ] Harness parameterized: no tailnet IP, no host name, no key path in tracked files.
- [ ] `git grep` for the tailnet range and `ssh pico` returns clean across tracked files.

title: setup: tutorial art direction — retrospective + /randomize composition plan + new-aesthetics research (images TABLED 2026-07-04)
description:

WHAT WE TRIED (submissions/2026-07-harness-loop-gateway/images/):
- Round 1 (8 styles of a goose piloting a biplane): retrofuturist-pop, aviation-deco, blueprint, flat-vector, risograph, watercolor, pop-comic, isometric-3D. Zig liked #1 (retrofuturist), #4 (flat-vector), #6 (watercolor), #8 (isometric).
- Round 2: refined those 4 + 4 blends. Zig initially liked the painterly diorama (b6x8) but ultimately rejected the diorama direction.
- Header pass (AAIF-recolor of the diorama): rejected -- colors bolder but not matching.
- Pivot: multi-ref (batch1 #1 + the AAIF ambassador logo), recolor to black+orange, pair the ambassador CHARACTER with the goose as a 'Where in the World is Carmen Sandiego' vigilante duo, strict NO-TEXT control. char = too extreme / black-on-black / illegible. char2 = legible full-palette (black+orange dominant + periwinkle/cream), better but still rejected.

WHAT WE LEARNED / DIDN'T LIKE (constraints for next time):
1. Black+orange must be DOMINANT but NOT the only colors -- need a full, legible palette (periwinkle, cream, sky tones, real value range). Pure black-on-black = illegible.
2. MASCOT FIDELITY (critical): the AAIF ambassador is an ALL-BLACK, FACELESS silhouette. Its ONLY facial feature is the round ORANGE monocle-lens; it also has a black trench coat, a black fedora with an orange hatband, and a small antenna with an orange tip. The generations wrongly gave it a face/eyes -- MUST prompt: faceless solid-black silhouette, no eyes, no visible face, monocle is the only feature.
3. Compositions got 'messy' / cluttered (busy space elements: planets, satellites, stars). Need cleaner, calmer compositions.
4. Text control WORKED when explicit ('absolutely no text/letters/numbers/symbols') -- keep that; add curated text only in post if wanted.

THE PLAN (when we return to images):
A. /randomize for NEW COMPOSITIONS -- don't reuse the single goose-in-biplane-in-sky comp Zig gave. Run /randomize over composition axes to force diversity, e.g.: SCENE (cockpit interior / on the tarmac / map-room war-table / rooftop stakeout / hangar / control tower / open sky), CAMERA (close two-shot / wide establishing / over-the-shoulder / low heroic / top-down), SUBJECT ARRANGEMENT (duo side-by-side / goose leading, agent following / back-to-back / conspiratorial huddle), MOOD (heist-caper / triumphant / sneaky-nefarious / cozy-partners), MEDIUM (flat vector / screenprint / gouache / cel / paper-cut), ERA-NOD (noir / 60s-spy / retrofuturist). Record the seed+provenance per /randomize discipline.
B. RESEARCH NEW AESTHETICS beyond the 8 tried -- candidates to explore: mid-century spy-thriller title-card (Saul Bass), Carmen-Sandiego cel-animation, noir woodcut, cut-paper/collage, gouache travel-poster, ligne-claire (Tintin), screenprint gig-poster, matte editorial vector. Pull Zig's cfp painterly refs (~/cfp/talk-ai-council/refs/msb-aesthetic) + the zig-voice mood-board + AAIF brand as image-to-image anchors.
C. KEEP: the character+goose DUO concept, the caper/vigilante energy, AAIF black+orange DOMINANT with legible support palette, faceless-black-mascot fidelity, strict text control.

Current best-legible asset: submissions/.../images/char2/a1-mascot.png (on metis ~/Downloads). Not final.
notes: CORRECTION to mascot fidelity (Zig 2026-07-04): the AAIF ambassador is NOT a faceless black silhouette (my earlier note was WRONG). It's a friendly cartoon secret-agent: a LIGHT/WHITE face with black cartoon line-features -- two eyes (one round with a highlight, one behind the round ORANGE dotted monocle-lens) and a big open smile -- under a black fedora, wearing a black trench coat with light lapels + buttons, an antenna with a ball tip on the hat, carrying an 'AAIF' briefcase, one white-gloved hand raised. KEY RULE: keep the FACE LIGHT with black features. Do NOT fill the character solid black -- that's the error that looked wrong. title: decision: pin tailscale out of the unattended brew upgrade on the gateway host
description:
Context: Zig chose "brew auto-upgrade all, like ubuntu.upgrade.sh" for the gateway
host's scheduled loop. `brew upgrade` restarts brew services, and tailscale is one
of them. The update loop reaches that host OVER the tailnet, and the gateway's own
llm provider targets ollama by tailnet address.

Alternatives considered: (a) upgrade everything including tailscale, as literally
asked; (b) hold brew at check-only until Zig watches a run; (c) upgrade all EXCEPT
the network dependency the automation itself rides on.

Decision: (c). `BREW_PIN` defaults to `tailscale`; pinned on the host now.

Why: a botched unattended tailscaled upgrade at 04:17 has a uniquely bad blast
radius — it would take the fleet's gateway offline AND remove the only remote way
to fix it, on a machine nobody is sitting at. Every other formula fails safely by
comparison. This preserves "auto-upgrade all" for the 47 other outdated formulas
rather than downgrading the whole class to check-only.

Reversibility: one command, either side — `brew unpin tailscale` on the host, or
`BREW_PIN=""` in the service env. Visible in `brew list --pinned`. Zero data risk.

Not escalated because it's a narrow, trivially reversible safety margin inside a
policy Zig already set, not a change of that policy. Flagged to him in the summary
so he can remove the pin if he'd rather upgrade it too.

title: setup: agentgateway auto-update loop for the pico gateway (staged, validated, auto-rollback)
description:
PROBLEM
The fleet's agentgateway deployment on the gateway host has NO upgrade mechanism.
v1.3.1 was hand-installed 2026-07-01 and has sat frozen: no crontab, no launchd
periodic job, no update script, not package-managed. The launchd plist only execs
the binary. agentgateway is a fast-moving AAIF project (v1.4.0-beta.1 tagged
2026-07-25) — the deployment will silently rot.

TWO UPSTREAM GOTCHAS a naive updater hits
1. GitHub /releases/latest returns v1.4.0-beta.1 with prerelease=false — upstream
   mis-flags prereleases. MUST filter stable by TAG-NAME semver, never the flag.
2. Config schema drifts between versions (the binary ships a `migrate` subcommand
   for deprecated local fields -> frontendPolicies). An upgrade can invalidate the
   live config.

SAFETY SURFACES THAT EXIST (verified live)
- `agentgateway -f <config> --validate-only` -> "Configuration is valid!" (the gate)
- readiness endpoint: readinessAddr -> /healthz/ready -> "ready" / HTTP 200
- guarded ports answer 401 unauthenticated (proves listener live AND authz loaded)
- per-release `<asset>.sha256` checksums; single static binary, atomic mv swap
- launchctl kickstart -k for a controlled restart; PID change proves real restart

DELIVERABLE
ops/agentgateway/ in this repo (source of truth, host-parameterized so no private
infra lands in the public repo):
- agentgateway-upgrade  : gateway-host script. check/apply/rollback/status.
  Staged swap: download+sha256 -> version self-check -> --validate-only against the
  LIVE config -> backup -> atomic mv -> kickstart -> health verify (readiness +
  version + PID changed + guarded ports still 401) -> AUTO-ROLLBACK on any failure.
- check-and-report.sh   : harness-side wrapper (schedules over ssh, reports into
  the harness: ledger + notification; files a bead when a human call is needed).
- deploy.sh + systemd unit templates (rendered locally; host never committed).

ACCEPTANCE
- `check` correctly reports current-vs-latest, ignoring mis-flagged prereleases.
- `apply` on an already-current deployment is a no-op, exit 0.
- A deliberately-bad staged binary/config triggers abort BEFORE the swap.
- A post-swap health failure auto-rolls-back and the gateway serves again.
- Timer installed; the loop is documented + the version pin in the /agentgateway
  skill points at the mechanism so it can't rot.
notes:
=== agentgateway ===
agentgateway-upgrade: BUILT + VERIFIED on a sacrificial instance; live gateway
untouched (PID 48645 unchanged throughout). v1.4.0-beta.1 validates against the
live config, so the 1.4.0 stable path is clean. Happy apply, manual rollback, and
a forced post-swap health failure with auto-rollback all pass.

=== CORRECTION: ollama WAS already supervised ===
My first diagnosis was WRONG and the wrong version was briefly recorded here.

I reported ollama as unsupervised/orphaned and one reboot away from taking local
inference down. The real supervisor is /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.zig.ollama.plist
(root:wheel, created 2026-06-12): RunAtLoad true, KeepAlive true, UserName pico,
all 7 OLLAMA_* vars pinned INCLUDING OLLAMA_HOST=<tailnet>:11434, program pointed
at the ollama-current symlink. So: it did start at boot, it did restart on exit,
and the tailnet binding was reproducible. Zig had set it up correctly.

Why I got it wrong: I checked only ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ and the gui/<uid>
domain, found the two genuinely-retired user-agent plists there, and concluded
"unsupervised." A system-domain job is INVISIBLE from gui/<uid> — print says
"Bad request", bootout says "No such process" — while the daemon keeps respawning,
which reads exactly like an unkillable ghost job. My one early check of the system
plist dirs was defeated by zsh aborting the whole command on the FIRST glob having
no match, so it never evaluated /Library/LaunchDaemons/*ollama*. The output read
as "no system-level plists". An error read as no-data.

COST: I created a duplicate user LaunchAgent (com.zig.ollama-serve) for a service
the daemon already supervised. They fought over port 11434 -> 32 bind errors and
TWO failed upgrade attempts. Removed; host verified back to a single supervisor
(system daemon, active count 1, PID == port holder, API + real inference healthy).

What WAS genuinely worth fixing: ~/ollama.log at 1.4 GB unrotated (truncated, tail
kept as .prev), and the 9-stable-release staleness with no upgrade mechanism.

=== The updater behavior this validated (the useful part) ===
Through both environmental failures the updater never claimed success it could not
observe (version-match + new-PID + real-inference all had to hold), rolled back to
a known-good version both times, and said MANUAL INTERVENTION REQUIRED loudly when
rollback itself could not be verified. A blind `curl -o` updater would have swapped
the binary, exited 0, and reported success with the inference backend down.

=== launchd gotchas now encoded in the scripts + README ===
1. A system-domain job is invisible from gui/<uid>. Check EVERY domain and
   /Library/LaunchDaemons before concluding anything about supervision.
2. `launchctl bootout` returns success but can leave a pending spawn that fires
   seconds later, grabs the port, and turns the next bootstrap into a bind-error
   respawn loop. Restart with `kickstart -k`; to truly stop: disable -> bootout ->
   drain to verified quiet.
3. `KeepAlive:{SuccessfulExit:false}` is wrong for a server restarted via
   `kickstart -k`: the graceful kill exits 0, launchd calls it done and refuses to
   restart. Test supervision with SIGTERM, not just kill -9, or the broken path
   passes.
4. ppid 1 is not "detached" — launchd IS pid 1. Use XPC_SERVICE_NAME to attribute.
5. A zsh glob with no match aborts the WHOLE command; later paths never evaluate.

=== Separate real bug found + fixed (dotfiles-6uj) ===
~/dotfiles/ubuntu.upgrade.sh installed agentgateway from /releases/latest/download/,
which resolves to v1.4.0-beta.1 (prerelease mis-flagged false upstream). It had
ALREADY put that beta on zig-computer at 04:11 today. Now semver-stable +
sha256-verified + temp-file staged; zig-computer reverted to stable v1.3.1. Nothing
served it there -> no live impact.

# SPEC — August anchor: "the gateway is the ledger"

> Bead: aaif-51g. Contract: `SOURCES.md` in this folder. Folder is GITIGNORED.

---

## 1. Angle-lock (the thesis, three sentences)

A fleet of agents produces two things nobody can read from the client side: an
economy and a record, and every layer that could describe them is the same layer
that could be wrong about them. One agentgateway process sitting between the fleet
and the model API is the only seam that can answer both honestly -- it meters spend
per seat and per subscription pool via CEL-mapped request headers, and it issues the
MCP toolset scope each agent gets, so "who spent what" and "what was that agent even
allowed to touch" come out of the same log. Steve Yegge's August essays name the
token tap and the principle "never falsify the record" without a mechanism for
either; the mechanism is a gateway, and this piece shows it measured twice -- in
production attribution, and in a 24-cell toolset ablation where the lean,
gateway-issued toolset is both the cost minimum and the productivity maximum.

title: idea: 'Two gateways, two problems' — LiteLLM vs agentgateway explainer + decision guide
description:
ANGLE: a clarifying explainer answering the question every dev evaluating agentgateway asks — "how is this different from LiteLLM, which has ~10x the GitHub stars?" Frame = "two gateways, two problems," NOT "agentgateway beats LiteLLM." Genuinely fair to LiteLLM (best-in-class LLM proxy). Origin: Zig hit this exact question himself 2026-07-11.

THESIS: LiteLLM and agentgateway overlap on the LLM-proxy square but are shaped for different-sized problems from opposite starting points. LiteLLM = "call any of 100+ models through one OpenAI-compatible API + track the bill" (LLM-first; Python SDK + proxy; ~53k stars; the problem nearly everyone has today, and older). agentgateway = "govern + observe a whole agent fleet's traffic — LLM + MCP + A2A — as one network data plane" (protocol-plane-first; purpose-built Rust; ~3.5k stars; the problem that's arriving). The star gap measures problem-ubiquity + age, not quality — say so plainly.

DIFFERENTIATION AXES (the body):
1. CENTER OF GRAVITY — LLM-first vs protocol-plane. LiteLLM added MCP/A2A as endpoints; its MCP is LLM-endpoint-centric (register servers, call tools THROUGH /chat/completions). agentgateway treats LLM/MCP/A2A as peers over one data plane; virtual-MCP federation (multiplex many MCP servers into one endpoint, tool-name prefixing, per-tool CEL authz, unauthorized tools filtered out of `list` entirely = tool-poisoning defense) is the deepest MCP support in the space. "LiteLLM is an LLM gateway that learned some MCP; agentgateway is an agent-traffic gateway where MCP is first-class."
2. ARCHITECTURE — Python library-that-grew-a-proxy vs purpose-built Rust data plane. Load-bearing rationale: MCP's stateful, bidirectional streaming mismatched the stateless model of existing proxies (Envoy) -> they built a new one; hence Gateway-API-conformant, mTLS, xDS hot-reload (real network infra, not an app-tier service). PERF: vendor benchmarks ~11.5x throughput / ~10x lower latency / 22MB vs 11.8GB memory. MUST cite as VENDOR-published (Solo.io / Lin Sun) AND link the reproducible repo (github.com/linsun/litellm-agw-perf) so readers can re-run; never launder as neutral fact.
3. GOVERNANCE — both do virtual keys / budgets / spend / guardrails (LiteLLM excellent at multi-tenant cost). agentgateway differentiator = uniform CEL authorization across ALL three protocols + the "kill-switch" posture (nothing reaches a model/tool except through the gateway; per-agent token budget + tool allowlist; one JWT revocation halts a rogue agent). LiteLLM governs spend + model access; agentgateway governs capability + blast radius.

DECISION GUIDE (a table): when LiteLLM (unify providers, Python app, multi-tenant spend, most mature here) vs when agentgateway (MCP tool governance, network-grade authz/mTLS/Gateway-API, fleet-wide enforcement/kill-switch, proxy-tier perf). Non-obvious closer: it's NOT strictly either/or — you can run LiteLLM as a provider behind agentgateway, or use each for the layer it's best at. If you only need the LLM-proxy third, LiteLLM is the pragmatic pick today.

HOOK / SPINE: convergence — both moving toward "the agentic gateway" from opposite ends (LiteLLM up from the LLM-proxy side adding MCP/A2A; agentgateway out from the network-data-plane side including LLM). "Where a tool starts reveals what it optimizes for." This is the concrete, accessible on-ramp to the aaif-715 "harness/loop/gateway are converging" perspective piece — could pair or feed it.

ANTI-SLOP GATES (before any publish):
- VENDOR-NEUTRAL: fair to LiteLLM (it's genuinely excellent at its job); "two problems," never "X beats Y"; no benchmark-war framing (they already published the benchmarks — echoing them reads as vendor slop).
- VERIFY (both move fast): benchmarks are vendor -> link repo, don't launder. Re-characterize LiteLLM's MCP/A2A support against CURRENT docs (ideally a hands-on check) before publish — the "MCP through /chat/completions" claim needs a fresh confirm. Confirm star / provider counts at publish time.
- REAL USAGE: Zig speaks first-person on the agentgateway side (real deploy on pico, the /agentgateway skill, the shipped yw5 tutorial). Don't assert LiteLLM first-person unless he actually runs it.

PREDICTED TYPE: blog_post (~15 pts). Tutorial-upside (20) IF it ships with a runnable side-by-side — the SAME fleet routed through each gateway. RADAR FIT (W28 scan): agentgateway explainer content is the MOST under-served lane while intro-MCP blogs are saturated -> high developer pull, low competition.

description:
GOAL: Re-architect the AAIF tutorial "If you give a Goose an MCP server" into a genuinely useful, substantive, technical-leader-respecting agentgateway tutorial; consolidate the 5 gateway-* skills into ONE agentgateway skill FIRST; then harden the draft via a subagent workflow; then ship to the review gist (after Zig's okay), gist FIRST then metis. Zig-directed after he rejected the v5 "nursery-rhyme" draft as over-whimsical, vaporous, and structurally gapped. Execute end-to-end in a FRESH session (this one is context-saturated); onboard reads this bead + .local/goose-tutorial-execution.md + the handoff note.

WHY (v5 gaps to fix):
1. NO model-setup step. The tutorial routes the local model through the gateway (the whole o11y point) yet never configures it. The real first step is configuring the model.
2. The MCP step never explains the actual move. It must teach: federate raw MCP servers as targets -> the gateway VIRTUALIZES them into ONE endpoint -> scope that endpoint per-key with CEL so each agent/session discovers only its allowed tools. That per-agent scoping is the core value and is currently absent.
3. Too much AI/whimsy language ("Here's the half most local setups skip"...); vaporous; not technical enough; would not earn a technical leader's respect. Dial whimsy WAY back.
4. Skills section buries real work. 5 is bloat; "watch" is misleading (a skill can't watch continuously); no examples of what each is or how they combine. -> ONE agentgateway skill with components + real usage examples.
5. Step 5 "parts that will trip you" -> CUT entirely.
6. "Why a gateway and not just a smaller server" -> false comparison (a gateway IS a server); bad header; useless copy -> CUT.
7. The "If You Give a Mouse a Cookie" conceit is MISUSED in places. Recognizable children's story; use it correctly. The FORMAT is good -> use it for the SECTION HEADERS / structure (the "zoom out" moves), not scattered cutesy lines.

SUBSTANCE TO TEACH (verified vs the live config + agentgateway docs; generic shapes here, private IPs/paths in .local):
- MODEL SETUP: agentgateway `llm` block = a `provider` (e.g. `provider: ollama`, `params.baseUrl: http://localhost:11434/v1`) + a `models:` list, each `provider: {reference: <name>}`. Register your local model -> model calls route through the gateway's LLM listener, so model calls AND tool calls land in the SAME request log. Be opinionated: "I'm using Ollama + qwen3:8b; use whatever you like." Fold the context-window reality here: small models default to a tight window (~4096 for qwen3:8b); raise with `num_ctx` / env `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` (~32768) or tool schemas overrun the context and the model silently stops calling tools.
- MCP VIRTUALIZATION + SCOPING (the spine): add each raw MCP server as a `target` (name + stdio cmd) under the `mcp` block = the federated pile. The gateway presents them as ONE virtual MCP endpoint (multiplexing). `mcpAuthorization` CEL rules scope per key: `apiKey.name == "goose" && mcp.tool.name in [read_text_file, write_file, edit_file, list_directory, search_files, fetch]` grants exactly six; a broader key (cc) sees all. Unauthorized tools are FILTERED from tools/list (the client never discovers them). Give each agent/session its own key -> per-agent/per-session tool scoping off one virtual server. tiny-tools = the goose key's 6-tool view. Docs: https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/tutorials/mcp-federation/ | https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/main/mcp/mcp-authz/ | https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/latest/mcp/virtual/
- FACTS TO PRESERVE (fact-checked, do not re-break): filesystem server = 14 tools, NO delete tool; write_file overwrites (the destructive one, KEPT because the task writes files); move_file "fails if destination exists" (does NOT overwrite; CUT for task-need not danger); fetch = 1 tool; federated = 15; keep 6; move_file probe -> status=400 "Unknown tool: filesystem_move_file"; access-log (tool calls) vs request-log DB (model calls) split; agentgateway self-describes as "connectivity solution / proxy," NOT "data plane" (don't overclaim). Full list + config shapes: .local/goose-tutorial-execution.md.

RE-ARCHITECTURE (substance-first; longer is fine; doc links where they help; zero cutesy filler; title kept as the hook; nursery-rhyme = correct light touch in the SECTION HEADERS/structure only):
  1. Put your model behind the gateway (provider + model; opinionated Ollama+qwen3:8b; num_ctx/context window here). NEW; needs a Models-view screenshot (redact the ollama IP -> localhost).
  2. Federate your MCP servers into one virtual endpoint (targets -> one endpoint).
  3. Scope the endpoint per agent (per-key CEL; unauthorized tools vanish; the CORE value; tiny-tools = goose's cut).
  4. Watch it all in one place (model + tool calls in one log — the payoff of routing both).
  5. Prove the scope holds (move_file -> "Unknown tool" probe).
  6. One agentgateway skill (audit/cost/trace/harden as components + the request-log cookbook reference; real examples of running them as a loop; DROP "watch").
  + Team-scale closer (per-agent scoping -> role-scoped keys). CUT the gotchas step + the "why a gateway vs a server" section.

PHASE 0 — SKILLS CONSOLIDATION (do FIRST): merge aaif/.claude/skills/gateway-{audit,cost,watch,trace,harden} into ONE `agentgateway` skill. Keep audit/cost/trace/harden as documented components; DROP "watch"; the request-log cookbook (refs/gateway-request-log-cookbook.md) is the shared reference. Include real loop examples (audit the morning after -> trace a surprising call -> cost a heavy run -> harden proposes a tighter allowlist for review; read-only, human-gated, harden never applies). Update CLAUDE.md routing + file layout to one skill; update the tutorial's skill section to link it.

PHASE 1 — REWRITE (lead, grounded): produce the restructured, de-whimsied, substantive draft. Capture the new Model-setup screenshot(s) from the live gateway UI (rig + redaction in .local). Reuse existing UI screenshots (servers, tools, tool-call) where they fit.

PHASE 2 — WORKFLOW HARDENING (use the Workflow tool; Zig-directed): parallel fresh-eyes critiques on the Phase-1 draft, each a distinct lens: (a) technical-leader-respect (substantive + accurate? would a staff/principal engineer respect it?); (b) GPT-ism/AI-language audit (list every tell; zig-voice banned list); (c) helpfulness (can a reader DO this end to end? what's under-explained/missing?); (d) voice x2 — one pass WITH /zig-voice, one WITHOUT; (e) STORY FIDELITY — a dedicated agent reading the piece against "If You Give a Mouse a Cookie" to verify the conceit is used CORRECTLY (not misused) and to propose using the format for the section headers/structure. Then a SYNTHESIS agent merges into a hardened rewrite; then a FINAL COLD READ (fresh agent, no prior context). Verify EVERY technical claim survives; no GPT-isms; story correct.

DELIVERY: land in the gist once ready. Order: Zig reviews -> okay -> push to the GIST FIRST -> THEN the metis Obsidian vault (blog). Paths/frontmatter in .local. Gist must render all images.

[ ] Whimsy = correct light nursery-rhyme touch in headers/structure; body substantive + technical; opinionated stack; doc links where they help; zero cutesy filler.

title: fix: /amplify's standalone-5pt verdict must apply the W32 'amplification without substance' rejection rule
description:
## Context

The W32 radar scan (aaif-ecw) discovered a NEW rejection rule in the automated reviewer's
grading model, and it lands squarely on /amplify's job.

THE RULE (observed on a rejected submission, W32): a social post that promotes an event or
release but carries 'no technical explanation, practical guidance, or another developer-useful
resource' is REJECTED outright -- no scorecard, zero points. Verbatim: 'Social submissions need
more than event promotion or general amplification to qualify.'

WHY IT MATTERS HERE. /amplify's contract includes answering 'does this stand alone as its own
5-pt pulse contribution?' The default announcement thread -- 'I published X, here's the link,
tagging @AgenticAIFdn #AAIFAmbassador' -- is EXACTLY the shape this rule rejects. Submitting
one is not a 0-value move, it's a rejection on the record.

THE MODEL, RESTATED: the 5 points on social_thread are for DEVELOPER VALUE, not for posting.
A thread qualifies only if it teaches something that stands on its own WITHOUT the artifact it
points at -- i.e. a reader who never clicks through still learned a technical thing.

The rule is already folded into the public /aaif-review skill and the private grading notes
(same run, per the radar fold-back rule); this bead covers the second consumer.
